title: Adversarial external id: both /api/attachment/[id] routes read another tenant's attachment with no tenant scope and an institution-blind ACL
why_open: Still open, and re-verified against the current tree after the §16 work landed. apps/web/src/lib/messaging.ts:31 `canReadConversation(ctx, convo)` still takes exactly two arguments and its OSE_BROADCAST arm at messaging.ts:36-40 is `isOse(ctx, convo.institutionId) || ctx.orgRoles.some((r) => r.status === 'ACTIVE' || r.status === 'SHADOW')` — the second clause never compares the reader's institution to `convo.institutionId`, and it cannot, because OrgRole (apps/web/src/lib/rbac.ts) carries no institutionId. Every other arm IS bound to an institution or to participants (BOARD_CHANNEL messaging.ts:35, APPROVAL_THREAD :42, DIRECT_MESSAGE via the participant short-circuit at :32), which isolates this as the one hole. The two routes that consume it are the two with no tenant scope at all: apps/web/src/app/api/attachment/[id]/route.ts:22 does `db.attachment.findUnique({ where: { id } })` and calls the helper at :36 with no `withTenantScope` imported anywhere in the file (imports at :1-6), and apps/web/src/app/api/attachment/[id]/content/route.ts:26/:40 is the same shape — its own comment at :11 states it copies the download route's ACL, so the defect is duplicated by design. The chokepoint cannot save either: Attachment is listed UNENFORCEABLE at apps/web/src/lib/tenancy/registry.ts:123 (`reachableVia: 'Message -> Conversation.institutionId'`), so scope-args adds no predicate even under TENANCY_ENFORCE=true. The third consumer, apps/web/src/app/(app)/messages/[id]/page.tsx:90, IS inside `withTenantScope` (page.tsx:64) and so already has an institution to pass — it just is not passing one. Net effect: a signed-in user at institution A holding any ACTIVE/SHADOW seat downloads institution B's broadcast attachment from a guessed id. apps/web/src/lib/messaging.test.ts:35-78 uses a single institution constant throughout and asserts no cross-institution denial anywhere.
smallest_real_change: Give `canReadConversation` the acting institution instead of letting it infer one. Change the signature to `canReadConversation(ctx, convo, actingInstitutionId)` and make the FIRST line `if (convo.institutionId !== actingInstitutionId) return false`, ABOVE the participant short-circuit currently at messaging.ts:32 — otherwise a cross-tenant participant row still walks through. One early return binds all four arms rather than patching OSE_BROADCAST alone, and it needs no schema change. The third parameter must be REQUIRED, not optional: an optional acting institution that a route forgets to pass compiles, keeps messaging.test.ts green because that file builds its own fixtures, and leaves the hole exactly where it is. `tsc` will then name all three construction sites — route.ts:36, content/route.ts:40, page.tsx:90 — and those are the three I checked; grep `canReadConversation` before landing to confirm no fourth has appeared. Wrap both attachment routes in `withTenantScope(session.user.id, async (scope) => ...)` (purpose 'interactive', which apps/web/src/lib/tenancy/context.ts:61 now requires) and pass `scope.institutionId`; page.tsx already has a scope at :64 and only needs the id threaded out of it. Do the same for `canPostToConversation` in the same edit — it has the identical institution-blind shape at messaging.ts and widening one without the other leaves a write hole behind a closed read hole. Tests in messaging.test.ts: build a conversation at inst_b and a ctx whose only orgRole is ACTIVE at an inst_a club, then assert `false` for all four conversation types including DIRECT_MESSAGE-with-participant. Mutation proof on the HELPER: delete the `convo.institutionId !== actingInstitutionId` line -> all four assertions must FAIL; restore -> PASS. Mutation proof on the PRODUCER (the one that matters, because a helper-only test stays green when a route stops calling it): in apps/web/src/app/api/attachment/[id]/route.ts pass `convo.institutionId` instead of `scope.institutionId` -> the route-level itest must FAIL. Add that end-to-end case to apps/web/src/lib/tenancy/isolation.itest.ts against the running Postgres so the proof is against the real database and the real route handler, and run `npm run test:isolation` (185 tests) since both routes are on a request path.

title: Relay answers are neither citation-verified nor current: SearchDoc still carries no timestamp and the model's answer is returned unchecked
why_open: Two of this gate's four clauses have no representation in code, and the recent WRK-010-003 work did not touch either. 'Current enough': apps/web/src/lib/search.ts:9-29 `SearchDoc` is `{ id, kind, title, body, href, context, mode }` — `mode` (the projection policy) was added, but there is still no `occurredAt`/`updatedAt`/`asOf` field, and `grep asOf` across search.ts, search-data.ts and apps/web/src/app/api/ai/chat/route.ts returns nothing at all. The five builders in apps/web/src/lib/search-data.ts (memory :125, document :148, approval :172, event :189, organization :204) each select a narrow field list (:58, :72, :78, :88, :99) that includes no timestamp column, so nothing downstream can say how old a retrieved passage is, refuse a stale one, or show freshness. The Bible is explicit that this is required: line 244 'Never answer as though a stale, deleted, inaccessible, or reconciliation-failed source is current. Show freshness and uncertainty', and line 725 describes the flagship accelerator as returning 'a synthesized answer with source/freshness'. 'Cited': chat/route.ts:351-359 instructs the model to 'Cite every claim with its source number in brackets, e.g. [1]' and then returns `answer` verbatim at :363-364 with no post-hoc check that the bracketed numbers exist in the offered set — an answer citing [7] against 6 sources, or citing nothing at all, ships to the user as a grounded answer. `sources` at :271-276 is projected as title/href/kind/context only, so even the client cannot render recency. Every clause of this gate is currently a prompt string rather than a control.
smallest_real_change: (1) Add a REQUIRED `asOf: Date` to `SearchDoc` at apps/web/src/lib/search.ts:9, for exactly the reason the neighbouring `mode` field's own doc block already gives (search.ts:14-27): required means `tsc` enumerates every construction site instead of an unset field failing only in production. The sites are the five builders in search-data.ts (:125, :148, :172, :189, :204) plus the fixture helper in search.test.ts, and each already has a column to select — `updatedAt` on MemoryRecord/Document/Organization, `createdAt` on ApprovalRequest, `startsAt` on Event — so each `select:` at :58/:72/:78/:88/:99 gains one field. Grep `SearchDoc` and `ScoredDoc` and fix every one in the same change; those six are the ones I checked. (2) New exported `verifyCitations(answer: string, sourceCount: number): { cited: number[]; invalid: number[] }` in search.ts, and in chat/route.ts refuse between :351 and :363 to return an answer whose `invalid` list is non-empty — replace it with the sources-only response the route already produces for the no-key case, reported through a separately-named field beside the existing `aiDisabledReason` / `connectorRefusal` / `toolRefusal` (that route already refuses to collapse distinct causes, so do not collapse this one either). (3) Project `asOf` into the `sources` array at chat/route.ts:271-276 so the client can show freshness, and refuse to include in `sourceBlock` any doc whose `asOf` is older than a stated staleness bound. Tests in search.test.ts: `verifyCitations('per [1] and [7]', 6)` returns invalid [7]; `verifyCitations('no citations here', 6)` returns cited []. Mutation proof on the PRODUCER, not the helper: in chat/route.ts change the guard to return the answer regardless of `invalid` -> the route test asserting a fabricated-citation answer is suppressed must FAIL; restore -> PASS. Proving this by calling `verifyCitations` directly is the exact fake this bar forbids — it stays green the moment the route stops calling it. Second mutation: drop `asOf` from the document builder in search-data.ts -> `tsc` must fail, which is the whole point of making the field required.

title: The document graph records no binding between the WRK Bible and the eight authorities it defers to
why_open: Re-verified: `grep -n 'binds\|defers\|owned_by' docs/architecture/architecture-document-graph.yaml` returns NOTHING — the schema has no such field on any document. The WRK entry at docs/architecture/architecture-document-graph.yaml:506-520 carries only `superseded_by`, `supersedes: []`, `aliases: []` and `requirement_prefixes: [WRK]`. The Bible states the bindings in prose that a generator could read today: Tenure_Universal_Work_Graph_and_Workspace_Connector_Cloud_Claude_Bible_v1.0.md:26-34 is a numbered list under '## 0. Constitutional relationship and ownership' naming the Constitution, the Master Prompt, the Integration Bible, the Tenant UX Bible, the Configurator Bible, the Global System Architecture Bible, the owning domain Bibles and the Connector Catalog; :49 then states the ownership split ('The Integration Bible continues to own the shared connector SDK/runtime ... Domain Bibles own the meaning and invariants of Finance, HCM, ...'). Nothing machine-readable connects the two, so nothing can detect that a WRK requirement was resolved against an authority that has since been retired — and the graph proves that case is live, not hypothetical: the Simon entry at :506-512 already carries a non-null `superseded_by`. tests/architecture/document-graph.test.mjs (244 lines) cannot assert a binding it has no field to read. This is one of the few WRK items that needs no provider, no AWS and no external decision, and it touches none of the files another run owns.
smallest_real_change: Extend tools/document-graph.mjs (578 lines) to extract, per authority, the numbered list under its 'Constitutional relationship' / 'Read completely before material implementation' heading — for WRK that is lines 26-34 — and emit it as `binds: [<document id>, ...]` on each document entry, resolving each prose name to a canonical document id through the same family/alias table the generator already builds. A name the table cannot resolve must be emitted as an explicit `unresolved` entry rather than silently dropped, because a binding list that quietly loses its unmatched rows is a binding list that always passes. Then add two assertions to tests/architecture/document-graph.test.mjs: (a) every id in every `binds` list resolves to a document present in the graph and no `unresolved` entries remain, and (b) no `binds` entry points at a document whose `superseded_by` is non-null — a requirement resolved against a retired authority is the exact failure this edge exists to catch, and the Simon entry proves the retired case is reachable. Regenerate the yaml with the generator (it is marked 'Do not edit by hand' at line 1 — do not hand-edit it, or the next regeneration silently reverts the work) and record the evidence in the ledger entry at docs/implementation/universal-work-graph-execution-ledger.md:53. Mutation proof on the GENERATED artefact the ledger cites, not on a helper: change one name in the Bible's binding list at line 30 to a Bible that does not exist in the repo, regenerate -> the resolution assertion must FAIL naming that document; restore -> PASS. Second mutation: point one `binds` entry at the Simon document, which already has a non-null `superseded_by` -> the retired-authority assertion must FAIL; restore -> PASS. Run `npm run test:platform`, which is where the architecture suite lives.

title: Seven of the eight sync primitives do not exist: only the outbound half was built
why_open: The outbound half genuinely landed since the last survey and must NOT be redone — apps/web/src/lib/outbox/prisma-ports.ts implements `OutboxPorts` over `db.outboxEvent`, apps/web/src/app/api/jobs/outbox/route.ts:87-99 is the runner (`forEachInstitution` + `dispatchOnce` + `gaps`), apps/web/src/lib/outbox/consumers.ts is the delivery end, and apps/web/src/lib/outbox/dispatch.itest.ts and apps/web/src/lib/jobs/outbox-dispatch.itest.ts prove it against real Postgres. The other seven named primitives have no implementation anywhere. `ls apps/web/src/app/api` shows exactly one inbound event receiver on the platform, `payments/provider-events`, which belongs to PAY and to no connector — there is no webhook or change-hint receiver for the work graph. There is no cursor/delta/history reader: apps/web/src/lib/search-data.ts loads its whole corpus with unbounded `findMany` selects (:58, :72, :78, :88, :99) and holds no cursor or checkpoint. There is no backstop poll (the only polling job is api/jobs/reminders and api/jobs/slo), no snapshot, no backfill, no on-demand fetch and no file/feed primitive in apps/ or packages/. The ledger's own entry at docs/implementation/universal-work-graph-execution-ledger.md:436-459 says this precisely and says the item returns to the queue for the seven, not for the outbound half.
smallest_real_change: Do not attempt all seven — six of them have no provider to run against and would be shapes, which is the dead-code failure this bar forbids. Build the two that have a real production caller today and let the rest stay honestly FAIL. (1) CURSOR/DELTA/HISTORY, against Tenure's own records, with apps/web/src/lib/search-data.ts as the caller: `loadSearchCorpus` currently re-reads five whole tables on every question. Add a checkpoint type carrying `{ model, lastSeenAt, lastSeenId }` and a `readDelta(ports, checkpoint)` that pages by `(updatedAt, id)` with a strict tiebreak, so a row whose `updatedAt` equals the checkpoint's is neither re-read forever nor skipped — that off-by-one IS the primitive, and a test that only checks 'returns rows' proves nothing about it. Persisting the cursor needs a table; state in the result that this adds a migration under apps/web/prisma/migrations and DOES NOT hand-edit apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma beyond the one model, since a second run is in this tree. (2) BACKSTOP POLL, reusing the runner shape that already works: api/jobs/outbox/route.ts:97 already computes `gaps(ports, { now: at })` and reports `oldestOverdueByMs` at :120 — extend that job (not a new one) to re-enqueue any delta whose checkpoint has not advanced within its stated interval, so the backstop has the same bearer-token guard, the same `forEachInstitution` tenant scope and the same job envelope as the dispatcher. Tests: apps/web/src/lib/jobs/outbox-dispatch.itest.ts's sibling against real Postgres — write two rows sharing one `updatedAt`, read a delta, assert the second run returns the second row exactly once and then nothing. Mutation proof on the PRODUCER: change the cursor comparison from `(updatedAt, id) > (lastSeenAt, lastSeenId)` to `updatedAt > lastSeenAt` -> the equal-timestamp itest must FAIL by dropping a row; restore -> PASS. Second mutation: freeze the checkpoint so it never advances -> the backstop assertion in the job itest must FAIL by re-enqueuing forever. Report the remaining five primitives as FAIL with the reason, not as a partial pass.

title: The certification contract is a generic happy path: `capabilityProblems` checks exactly two clauses before a pack may claim AVAILABLE
why_open: This requirement's whole subject is 'the FULL certification contract, not a generic happy path', and the gate that stands between a pack and AVAILABLE checks two things. packages/provisioning/src/connector-capability.ts:124-159 `capabilityProblems` runs only when `capability.status === 'AVAILABLE' || 'DEGRADED'` (:131) and then emits at most two problems: `evidence-missing` when `claimIsUnproven([key], capability.evidenceRefs)` (:133-145) and `disagrees-with-artifact` when the catalog gate refuses the connector (:147-156). That is 'somebody cited something' and 'the artifact gate agrees' — one citation of any kind satisfies the first, so a pack citing a single smoke test passes the same gate as a pack that ran golden, negative, volume and failure suites. The Bible requires far more per capability: WRK-130-003 in the same document demands 'provider-specific golden/negative/volume/failure suites', §180 requires per-object tombstones/etag/deleted timestamps, and the Bible's line 17-19 note inside this very file states 'read and write are separately certifiable' while nothing checks that a write pack cited write evidence. The whole file is 172 lines. Every pack in packages/provisioning/src/provider-packs.ts is `PLANNED` today, so nothing is being wrongly claimed RIGHT NOW — but that is exactly why this is the moment to build the contract: the gate must exist before the first pack tries to advance through it, and today the first one to try passes on one citation.
smallest_real_change: Declare the contract as a list of named clauses and require one evidence ref per clause, per direction. Add `CERTIFICATION_CLAUSES` to packages/provisioning/src/connector-capability.ts — golden, negative, volume, failure/outage, throttling-and-deprecation, deletion-propagation, acl-change-propagation, scope-exactness — each a literal string, and change `evidenceRefs` from a flat list to `Record<CertificationClause, string[]>` so a missing clause is a missing KEY the compiler can see rather than a short array nobody counts. Then extend `capabilityProblems` (:124) to emit one `clause-unproven` problem per clause with no citation, keeping the two existing problems unchanged, and keep `claimIsUnproven` as the single implementation both `certificationState` in catalogs.ts and this function call (the file's own doc block at :44-45 states that one-implementation rule — do not add a second). Changing the shape of `evidenceRefs` is precisely the silent widening this bar warns about: grep `evidenceRefs` and `ConnectorCapability` across packages/provisioning and packages/platform-config and fix every construction site in the same change; the ones to check are provider-packs.ts (every `pack(...)` row), catalogs.ts's `certificationState`, and the fixtures in provisioning.test.ts and catalogs.test.ts. Do NOT touch packages/contracts, packages/finops, apps/system-studio or infrastructure/terraform — another run owns them; if a type must move into contracts, return FAIL naming that file instead. Tests in provisioning.test.ts: a capability at AVAILABLE citing only a golden run produces seven `clause-unproven` problems and is not usable; the same capability citing all eight produces none. Mutation proof on the PRODUCER: in provider-packs.ts advance one pack to AVAILABLE with a single citation -> tests/architecture/provider-packs-bind-requirements.test.mjs must FAIL naming that pack and the missing clauses; restore -> PASS. Second mutation: delete one clause from `CERTIFICATION_CLAUSES` -> the count assertion must FAIL, proving the list is load-bearing and not decoration.

title: No provider-specific authorization profile exists: the OAuth primitives are built for login only and no connector declares its flow
why_open: The generic primitives exist and are good — packages/identity/src/authorization-request.ts declares PKCE (`CHALLENGE_METHOD = 'S256'` :44, `validateVerifier` :64), state/nonce binding (`beginAuthorization` :236, `bindCallback` :340) and exact-return-path validation (`validateReturnPath` :117), and packages/identity/src/code-exchange.ts:105 `exchangeCode` is the backend exchange with a 60-second window (:96). All of it is written for the OIDC SIGN-IN flow. Nothing binds any of it to a connector: `grep -rln 'code_verifier|PKCE|code_challenge'` across packages, apps/web/src and modules returns ONLY files under packages/identity/src — no connector authorization route, no per-provider profile, and no `redirectUri` declared on any pack. packages/provisioning/src/provider-packs.ts declares every named provider (Microsoft, Google, Slack, Notion, Box, Zoom) as a `ProviderPackEntry` at `PLANNED` carrying `egressHosts` and `requestedScopes`, and carries no authorization endpoint, no token endpoint, no exact redirect path, no response_mode, and no account-verification rule. So 'exact redirects' and 'account verification' — the two clauses of this requirement that cannot be inherited from the generic flow, because they are per-provider facts — have no representation at all, and the packs can advance toward AVAILABLE without ever stating how a tenant would authorize them.
smallest_real_change: Declare the profile as data on the pack and make an existing gate read it, rather than writing a connect route for a provider nobody can call yet — a route with no reachable caller is the dead code this bar forbids. Add a required `authorization: ProviderAuthorizationProfile` to `ProviderPackEntry` in packages/provisioning/src/provider-packs.ts: `{ authorizeEndpoint, tokenEndpoint, redirectPath, responseType, requiresPkce: boolean, requiresNonce: boolean, accountVerification: 'id-token-claim' | 'userinfo-call' | 'admin-consent-grant', verifiedAccountClaim: string }`. Required, because every existing `pack(...)` row must answer it — that is the widening check, and the construction sites are every row in provider-packs.ts plus any fixture in provisioning.test.ts and catalogs.test.ts; grep `ProviderPackEntry` and `pack(` before landing. Then give it a real consumer instead of leaving it a declaration: extend the usability gate so a pack whose `authorization` fails the contract cannot leave PLANNED — `requiresPkce === false`, an `authorizeEndpoint`/`tokenEndpoint` host not present in the pack's own `egressHosts`, a `redirectPath` that `validateReturnPath` from @tenure/identity rejects, or an `accountVerification` of `id-token-claim` with an empty `verifiedAccountClaim` each become a `UsabilityReason`. Reusing `validateReturnPath` (packages/identity/src/authorization-request.ts:117) rather than writing a second redirect validator is deliberate: two redirect rules that disagree is how an open redirect ships. Tests in provisioning.test.ts: a pack declaring an authorize endpoint on a host outside its `egressHosts` is refused with that named reason; a pack with `requiresPkce: false` is refused. Mutation proof on the PRODUCER: in provider-packs.ts set `requiresPkce: false` on the Microsoft pack -> the gate test must FAIL naming that pack; restore -> PASS. Second mutation: point one pack's `redirectPath` at `https://evil.example/cb` -> the `validateReturnPath` assertion must FAIL, which also proves the identity validator is genuinely wired and not just imported. Coordinate with WRK-100-004 above — both edit connector-capability.ts and provider-packs.ts and should be done by one agent in one pass.

title: Tool arguments are unvalidated by construction: the taxonomy landed but there is still no schema of any kind
why_open: Half of this landed and must not be redone: apps/web/src/lib/relay-tools.ts now derives a seven-value `ActionRiskClass` from the registration (`riskOf`, and it is the first reader of `readOnly` on the platform), `authorizeRelayTools` takes a required `allow: 'read-only' | 'any'`, and three gates run in order — surface ceiling, the tool's own permission, then the owning domain's policy via `owningPolicyPermission`. What is still entirely absent is the OTHER noun in the requirement, 'with schemas'. `ToolRegistration` carries no input or output schema field, so `invokeRelayTool` in relay-tools.ts can only check argument NAMES — it refuses `CALLER_DECIDED_ARGUMENTS` (tenantid/institutionid/connectionid/accountid/apikey/onbehalfof), demands a `confirmationToken` for a writing tool, and checks recipient arguments against an allow-list — and then passes every other key through untouched in `args: { ...proposal.args, tenantId, actorId }`. A model can therefore send any type, any extra field and any value for any argument the deny-list does not name, and nothing validates it. The ledger states the same conclusion at docs/implementation/universal-work-graph-execution-ledger.md:280-305 and names the obstacle: the schema field belongs on `ToolRegistration` in packages/contracts/src/index.ts.
smallest_real_change: packages/contracts is owned by a concurrent run, so the schema field CANNOT be added to `ToolRegistration` in this change and that must be reported as FAIL naming packages/contracts/src/index.ts rather than edited around. What is fully implementable inside the files above, and closes the reachable hole today, is to flip `invokeRelayTool` from a deny-list to an allow-list. Declare the argument contract in apps/web/src/lib/relay-tools.ts as `TOOL_ARGUMENT_SCHEMAS: Record<string, Record<string, 'string' | 'number' | 'boolean'>>` keyed by `toolKey`, seeded with the one real registration `search.corpus` from modules/index.ts, and make `invokeRelayTool` refuse (a) any tool key with no schema entry — failing closed, so the next registration somebody adds cannot be invoked until its arguments are declared, which is the opposite of today where an undeclared tool is fully permissive — and (b) any argument name not in the schema, or present with the wrong `typeof`. Keep the existing `CALLER_DECIDED_ARGUMENTS` check ABOVE the new one so a proposal naming `tenantId` still gets its specific refusal rather than a generic 'unknown argument', because those are two different things to tell somebody and the file's own design already refuses to collapse them. Reuse the existing `proposalRefusal` helper so the refusal carries the same `disclosure`/`safeReason`/`remedy` triple WRK-030-001 established. Tests in relay-tools.test.ts: a proposal carrying an undeclared `limit` argument is refused with `remedy.kind === 'PROPOSAL_NOT_ACCEPTED'` and `rejected === 'limit'`; a proposal whose declared argument has the wrong type is refused; a registration absent from the schema table is refused even when offered. Mutation proof on the PRODUCER: in modules/index.ts add a second tool registration and leave it out of the schema table -> the route test in ai-kill-switch.test.ts asserting it cannot be invoked must FAIL if the fail-closed branch is removed; restore -> PASS. Second mutation: change the unknown-argument branch to log instead of refuse -> the undeclared-`limit` assertion must FAIL. Record in the ledger that the contract-level half is FAIL and why, naming the file.

title: The ten work accelerators have no declared existence, and nothing computes which connector capabilities are 'selected for release'
why_open: The Bible enumerates the accelerators at Tenure_Universal_Work_Graph_and_Workspace_Connector_Cloud_Claude_Bible_v1.0.md:721-736 ('## 11. High-value end-to-end work accelerators', beginning '1. Cross-app answer with citations: Search allowed Tenure records, email, chat, docs, meetings, tasks, and knowledge; return a synthesized answer with source/freshness and access-safe deep links'), and `grep -n accelerator` across the whole repo outside that Bible and the ledger returns nothing — no type, no list, no gate. The clause that makes this checkable rather than aspirational is 'for the exact connector capabilities selected for release', and no such set is computed anywhere: every row in packages/provisioning/src/provider-packs.ts is `PLANNED` with `PLANNED` capabilities, and `availabilityDecisions` returns `planned` for all of them, so the set selected for release is currently EMPTY. Nothing states that, so nothing stops a console, a doc or a marketing claim asserting an accelerator that rests on a connector nobody built — which is the overstatement WRK-GATE-000 and WRK-130-005 exist to prevent, and the failure mode the provider-packs file's own doc block (:20-25) already describes for lifecycle rows.
smallest_real_change: Declare the ten as data with their capability dependencies, and compute their availability rather than asserting it. Add `WORK_ACCELERATORS` to packages/provisioning — ten entries transcribed from the Bible's §11 list, each `{ key, title, requiresCapabilities: readonly string[] }` where each string is a `capabilityKey(...)` from connector-capability.ts:104 — and an `acceleratorAvailability(accelerators, capabilities)` that returns, per accelerator, either `available` or `unavailable` naming EVERY capability it needs that is not `AVAILABLE`. With the catalog as it stands today that function must return ten `unavailable` verdicts, and a test asserting exactly that is the honest state of the platform written down where it can red when somebody overstates it. Do not claim accelerator 1 as done because the chat route exists: it retrieves only Tenure's own records, and the accelerator's text names email, chat, docs and meetings — asserting otherwise is the false PASS this bar forbids. Add the assertion to tests/architecture/provider-packs-bind-requirements.test.mjs, which already parses provider-packs.ts as text and already fails when a pack's lifecycle disagrees with its requirement's ledger status, so the accelerator check inherits a proven harness rather than starting a second one. Do NOT edit apps/system-studio to render this — another run owns that tree; if the console needs the verdict, return FAIL naming apps/system-studio. Mutation proof on the PRODUCER: in provider-packs.ts advance the capabilities behind accelerator 1 to `AVAILABLE` without evidence -> the WRK-100-004 clause gate must FAIL first (proving the two gates compose in the right order), and with evidence added the accelerator's verdict must flip to `available`, which the test asserts explicitly; restore -> PASS. Second mutation: delete one entry from `WORK_ACCELERATORS` -> the 'ten accelerators are declared' count assertion must FAIL, so the list cannot silently shrink to whatever is convenient. Same file area as WRK-100-004 and WRK-040-001; one agent should take all three.
